text:
A: Hello, can you hear me?
B: Hiya! Yes. I'm Blerta, from Newcastle.
A: Nikhil, Thornton Heath, South London. Er, I have to ask, the postcard on your corkboard, in the photo. The woodblock print. Is that Hokusai?
B: Oh, yes! Well, I think so. It's from a charity shop. I'm obsessed with Japan, sorry. I've got a spreadsheet of how much it'd cost to go.
A: A spreadsheet. That's very serious. I want to go as well. My wife and I keep saying next year and then it's Pune instead, to see my parents.
B: Same! I go back to Kosovo most summers for my nana, so the money goes there. Do you speak any Japanese?
A: None. I'm doing Portuguese on an app, fifteen minutes a day. My streak is at two hundred and something.
B: I'm doing Japanese on one! I'm terrible, though. I can say "I am a student" and "where is the station".
A: That's the important stuff, honestly. Where is the station. What are you studying?
B: Speech and language therapy, second year, Northumbria. I want to do stroke rehab, adults. What do you do?
A: CAD technician. Building services, so pipes and ducts and electrics on drawings. Less interesting than speech therapy, I think.
B: No, I think that's dead interesting, like, how buildings actually work inside. I always look at ceilings in hospitals and think, what's up there?
A: Mostly ducts and a lot of cables nobody labelled. That's my life. So why speech therapy, with the languages? You speak Albanian, you said?
B: Albanian at home, English everywhere else. And that's sort of why, actually. My aunties get assessed for things in English, and they understand maybe half, and then it goes in their notes like they're confused. And they're not confused, it's just the wrong language. So one day I'd like to make assessments in Albanian.
A: That's a very good reason. My parents have the same problem when they visit and need a doctor. My mother's English is fine but when she's worried it all goes, and she switches to Marathi.
B: Yes! It's exactly that. Stress takes the second language first. We did a lecture on it.
A: Huh. I didn't know that was a known thing. It makes sense.
B: Do you read in Marathi?
A: Less than I should. I read a lot of translated fiction, though, in English. Saramago at the moment, slowly.
B: Oh, I do that! Kadare, and loads of Japanese stuff from the library. Murakami, but I think everyone says Murakami. Have you read Convenience Store Woman?
A: No, should I?
B: Yes, it's short, it's weird, you'd finish it on the train.
A: The train, if Southern runs it. Okay, I'll look for it. And you should go to Lisbon before Tokyo, it's cheaper. I've been told by everyone in this study, I think.
B: Ha, Lisbon's on the spreadsheet as well, actually, it's on the second tab, with—
